name: page_drawn
title: A page the model draws: a line chart of daily calories and protein, the module's front

steps.say: track what I eat: a food log with the date, the item, calories and protein in grams
steps.reply:
I've made a **Food log** table in a new Food module. It has four fields: date, item, calories (kcal) and protein (g). It's empty so far.

Tell me what you eat, for example "had two eggs and toast for breakfast". I'll add a row dated today. If you don't give calories or protein, I'll estimate them and mark them as estimates. If you give the numbers, I'll use yours.
steps.routed_by: judge: A food log that keeps growing over time is a standing table kept current, and no open work item covers it.

steps.say: log these for the last week: Mon 12 Oct oats 350 kcal 12 g protein, chicken salad 520 kcal 42 g; Tue 13 Oct eggs 300 kcal 20 g, pasta 700 kcal 25 g; Wed 14 Oct yoghurt 200 kcal 15 g, steak 650 kcal 55 g; Thu 15 Oct toast 280 kcal 8 g, curry 800 kcal 30 g; Fri 16 Oct smoothie 320 kcal 18 g, pizza 900 kcal 35 g; Sat 17 Oct pancakes 450 kcal 10 g, salmon 600 kcal 45 g; Sun 18 Oct granola 400 kcal 12 g, soup 350 kcal 14 g
steps.reply:

steps.routed: Track what I eat: a food log with the date, the item,…
steps.routed_by: judge: The sentence logs 14 meals into the Food log table that the open item created, so it is about that item's subject and follows on from it.

steps.say: make a summary page for Food with a line chart of my daily calories and protein, one line each, and make it the page the module opens on
steps.reply:
I made a Summary page for Food and set it as the page the module opens on. I haven't opened it to look at it.

- **Chart:** a line chart with one line for daily calories and one for daily protein. The seven days (12–18 Oct) run along the bottom. Calories use the left axis (kcal). Protein uses the right axis (g). I gave them separate axes because protein would otherwise be squashed flat at the bottom. Hovering over a point shows its value.
- **Averages:** above the chart are the average calories per day, the average protein per day, and the number of days logged.
- **Updates:** the page reads f
steps.routed: Track what I eat: a food log with the date, the item,…
steps.routed_by: judge: The sentence changes what the food log item made, since the summary page charts the food_log data it already holds, though building a standing module page could also argue for a new item.
